transcript.text: Here's how I lost $50 million in an
actual deal. So, gym launch company that
we had before we sold to private equity,
it was growing well and then a
competitor came into my space, siphoned
the top 10 clients that I had, started
running ads with them. They offered like
one-on-one service and some higher level
stuff than what I was doing from a touch
basis, not from an ROI basis. But I got
frightened and scared and so then I
decided to change our offering, add all
the stuff that they were doing plus what
we were doing and then I said I was
going to cut my price. And so I did this
big launch and I told all my customers,
"Hey, guess what? I did this big stack."
And I was just like, "You're going to
get all this for less than you're
currently paying." And the first
response, I remember it like yesterday,
a lady says, "Wait, so I could have been
getting more for less this whole time?"
So, rather than being grateful,
literally the first thought people had
was like, "Wait, you were charging me
more than you could have been charging
me?" And so, from there it was like the
first step in the bad direction.
Immediately overnight, I lost $500,000 a
month in top line revenue that cut
straight out of my bottom line and I
never recovered that $6 million in
profit per year. And so, when I ended up
selling my company within the next two
years, that $6 million in profit would
have very much been $50 million plus at
point of sale. So, the big lesson I got
from that is that you should always
listen to your customers and never the
competitors because my business was
doing fine, I just got reactive, looked
at what someone else is doing rather
than keeping my eye on the ball and it
was one of the most painful lessons I
had to learn in my career.
